clean_tree_sfu_pause_repeat.scenario: The owned disposable SFU container was paused for 30 seconds and unpaused; CDP was disconnected during that interval. This is a media-server outage, not a Wi-Fi handover or a selective client network blackhole.
clean_tree_sfu_pause_repeat.after_unpause_observation: At the first post-unpause sample the peer was not connected and concealed samples had increased during outage. It reconnected, then packets, samples and audio energy increased across three intervals; one active peer remained and the live audio element was playing.

clean_tree_sfu_pause_120_seconds.scenario: Owned disposable SFU paused for 120 seconds and unpaused; CDP disconnected during outage. This tests media-server interruption, not Wi-Fi handover or selective client network loss.
clean_tree_sfu_pause_120_seconds.observations: Initial post-unpause peer sample was disconnected and concealed samples had increased. The peer reconnected, packets and audio energy grew in every subsequent interval, and one active peer and a playing live audio element remained. Recovery latency was not measured.

clean_tree_realtime_websocket_interrupti.environment: Android 15 API 35 emulator, Chrome 124.0.6367.219, listener only, synthetic Chromium sender, emulator -no-audio
clean_tree_realtime_websocket_interrupti.scenario: The page instrumentation closed application /api/v1/realtime WebSockets and immediately closed newly opened sockets for ten seconds; the isolated LiveKit SFU remained running. New sockets may briefly open before the handler closes them. The observation ended with zero open application realtime sockets, then the block was removed and an open socket was observed again.
clean_tree_realtime_websocket_interrupti.playback_after_realtime_reconnect: A live enabled unmuted audio track was attached to an unpaused unmuted audio element; three observed AudioContexts were running.
